QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_8

question.text: Per Table 4.4 in the chapter, which parameter most sharply differentiates a Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) from a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Minimum investment amount - SIF is INR 10 lakh across all strategies of the AMC; Cat III AIF is INR 1 crore
Issue process - SIF uses private placement; Cat III AIF uses public issue
Investor cap - SIF is capped at 1,000 investors; Cat III AIF has no cap
Sponsor commitment - SIF requires 5% of corpus or INR 10 crore; Cat III AIF has no such requirement

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 4.4 distinguishes a Specialised Investment Fund (SIF) from a Cat III AIF on minimum investment amount: an SIF requires INR 10 lakh across all strategies of the AMC, while a Cat III AIF requires INR 1 crore. The table also positions SIF as a public-issue product with no investor cap, contrasted with Cat III's private placement and 1,000-investor cap, and notes Cat III sponsor/manager commitment. The Trap: Option B inverts the issue process. Option C inverts the investor caps. Option D wrongly states that Cat III has no sponsor/manager commitment. Note: The workbook's Table 4.4 supports the INR 10 lakh SIF minimum investment versus the INR 1 crore Cat III minimum, SIF public issue versus Cat III private placement, no SIF investor cap versus the Cat III 1,000-investor cap, and Cat III sponsor/manager commitment.
